title: 2010 AMC 12A Problem 21
statement: The graph of \(y=x^6-10x^5\) \(+29x^4-4x^3+ax^2\) lies above the line \(y=bx+c\) except at three values of \(x,\) where the graph and the line intersect. What is the largest of those values?

solutions.text:
Let \(f(x)\) be the graph minus the line. It is nonnegative and vanishes at three points, each a double root, so \[f(x)=\big(x^3-Ax^2+Bx-C\big)^2.\]

Matching coefficients gives \(-2A=-10\Rightarrow A=5,\) then \(A^2+2B=29\Rightarrow B=2,\) then \(-2C-2AB=-4\Rightarrow C=-8.\)

Thus the cubic is \(x^3-5x^2+2x+8\) \(=(x+1)(x-2)(x-4),\) with roots \(-1,2,\) and \(4.\) The largest is \(4.\)

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: The graph minus the line is nonnegative with three double roots, so it equals \(\big((x-p)(x-q)(x-r)\big)^2\)
Match the coefficients of \(x^5,x^4,x^3\) to determine the cubic, then factor it
